full_opus_relabel_disposition: Single disagreeing hand (HU-6.5: Opus FOLD vs Sonnet 3-2 majority CALL); per dispatch §'Consensus rule' 3-2-with-research-contradicting-majority clause: HU-6.5 routed to owner-arbitration (consensus_action set to null in consensus.jsonl). Additional Opus runs not dispatched — single Opus disagreement on a 3-2-split spot is sufficient signal for owner-arbitration; further Opus voting would not change the underlying ambiguity.

reasoning: Drawing bucket — bare near-nut spade FD (Js, no Ace blocker) + wheel gutshot ≈ 12 outs (~22% direct, one card to come) facing a polarised 75% turn barrel after flop check-call. HU spot (num_opponents=1, line 729 carve-out applies; DO NOT Rule 11 multiway predicates do not trigger). KB §1.7 RAISE carve-out fails: hero has near-nut FD but no canonical Ace-blocker, so check-raise lacks the blocker leg of the §1.7 conditions. v3.2 OVERRIDE air-threshold is 3-way-framed; HU fold equity is structurally higher (~60% vs ~36%), but without the nut blocker the polarised barrel range is too value-heavy to fold out and check-raise is high variance. CALL realises ~22% direct + implied odds when the spade arrives OOP (somewhat degraded but non-zero) plus 3 clean wheel-T outs; pot odds 30% are bridged by combined direct + implied. FOLD is too tight HU with 12 outs vs a polarised range that contains live bluffs hero beats trivially.

Air bucket with two clean overcards (K and Q, ~6 noisy outs) on 8h6h5c-2d turn after BTN flop check-back, BB checks turn. HU spot (num_opponents=1, line 729 carve-out applies; DO NOT Rule 11 does not trigger). Villain's check-call-flop-check-turn line caps range to weak-pair / busted-FD / give-up air; villain_top_pair_plus_pct in this composition is low and villain_air_pct is meaningfully high — the canonical delayed-c-bet/probe spot. Hero is IP with K-Q overcard blockers cutting villain's KQ/KT/QT pair-equity continuing combos. Per DO NOT Rule 4 we don't auto-c-bet IP, but the bet here is justified by the capped passive range + blocker effects + brick-turn fold equity, not by position alone. 33% solver-aligned small size targets the give-up range cheaply while preserving check-back optionality on hostile river runouts; 75% overbet is too thin without the nut hand structure to polarise into.

Air bucket with two clean overcards (A and J, ~6 noisy outs) + ace blocker on Tc7c3s-5d turn after BTN flop check-back, BB checks turn. HU spot (num_opponents=1, line 729 carve-out applies; DO NOT Rule 11 does not trigger). Hero is PFA + IP; flop check-back capped hero's range to medium showdown / give-up air, and BB's check-flop-check-turn caps BB's range to weak pair / busted-FD / give-up air with low villain_top_pair_plus_pct and meaningful villain_air_pct. A-blocker reduces BB's AT two-pair value combos and J-blocker reduces JT/J-x pair-equity combos — both prune the parts of BB's range that don't fold to a probe. 5d is a brick (no flush completion, no direct straight completion). Per DO NOT Rule 4 we don't auto-c-bet, but the delayed c-bet is supported by the passive line + blockers + brick. 33% solver-aligned small size captures the give-up fold equity cheaply and keeps showdown realisation viable when called; 75% overbet over-polarises a hand that prefers a thin probe.

Drawing bucket (combo) — 8-out OESD + 9-out second-nut FD (Th not Ah) ≈ ~15 outs and ~34% direct equity, BB OOP first-to-act on 9h7c2h before any c-bet. HU spot (num_opponents=1, line 729 carve-out applies; DO NOT Rule 11 does not trigger; KB §1.7 raise predicates concern facing-a-bet semi-bluff RAISE not first-action lead). Donk-leads on neutral-to-slightly-BB-favoured textures are a low-frequency solver mix; the dominant first-action solver line for OOP combo draws facing an uncapped IP opener is CHECK with the plan to check-call or check-raise the high-frequency c-bet that comes next. Checking preserves the option to take BTN's c-bet money via check-raise as a §1.7-style semi-bluff (combo draw + side equity) on the next node, and to realise equity passively via check-call against smaller sizings. Donk-leading sacrifices the fold equity that comes from raising a c-bet and conflates hero's range with the made-hand donk frequency. CHECK is the higher-EV first action; plan is to check-raise BTN's expected c-bet as semi-bluff with the combo draw or check-call smaller sizings to realise equity.

TP+ bucket — nut straight (5-6-7-8-9 with hero's 9h) but no flush on a flush-completing river (board 2d/8d, hero's Qd is a weak single diamond blocker, no Ad/Kd). HU spot (num_opponents=1, line 729 carve-out applies; DO NOT Rule 11 does not trigger). BB's line — check-call flop 25%, check-call turn 33% brick that added a BDFD (2d), then DONK-LEAD 150% on the 8d river that completes the flush — is the maximally polarised river action sequence. BB never raised; BB only acted aggressively when the flush arrived. This line on a flush-completing river is condensed to made flushes (any two-diamond combo that picked up the turn BDFD and rivered the flush) plus a thin bluff-frequency tail; the realistic value-vs-bluff distribution puts BB's bluff frequency well below the 37.5% pot-odds threshold required to break even. Hero's Qd diamond blocker is mediocre (not Ad/Kd) and does not meaningfully prune BB's nut-flush combos. The straight beats sets/two-pair/overpairs/9x but those combos rarely lead-overbet 150% on this runout — they more typically check-call or check-raise. Required equity 37.5% is not cleared on the realistic range distribution; FOLD.
